baseline: Comprehensive Rules effective 2026-08-07, retrieved 2026-09-10 (see RQ_C2_AUTHORITY_BASELINE.md). Excerpts are short quotations plus paraphrase; rule numbers are the citation of record.

101.4.excerpt: If multiple players would make choices and/or take actions at the same time, the active player makes any choices required, then the next player in turn order ... Then the actions happen simultaneously. ... often referred to as the 'Active Player, Nonactive Player (APNAP) order' rule.
101.4.proposition: Simultaneous multi-player choices/actions are ordered APNAP; later choosers know earlier choices (101.4b).

104.3a.excerpt: A player can concede the game at any time. A player who concedes leaves the game immediately.
104.3a.proposition: Leaving the game (concession) is always available; triggers 800.4 cleanup.

105.2.excerpt: An object is the color or colors of the mana symbols in its mana cost ... An object's color or colors may also be defined by a color indicator or a characteristic-defining ability.
105.2.proposition: Card color comes from mana-cost symbols/indicators/CDAs only. Basic lands have no mana cost: Island is COLORLESS, not a blue card (with 305.6).

108.3.excerpt: The owner of a card in the game is the player who started the game with it in their deck.
108.3.proposition: Ownership is fixed at game start; distinct from control (with 110.2).

110.2.excerpt: A permanent's owner is the same as the owner of the card that represents it ... A permanent's controller is, by default, the player under whose control it entered ...
110.2.proposition: Owner/controller split is normal (Reanimate: P0 controls P1-owned Bear).

111.3.excerpt: The spell or ability that creates a token may define the values of any number of characteristics for the token ... functionally equivalent to ... printed on a card.
111.3.proposition: Created tokens (Delina copy-token, Spirit token) take characteristics from the creating effect.

111.7.excerpt: A token that's in a zone other than the battlefield ceases to exist. This is a state-based action ... (Note that if a token changes zones, applicable triggered abilities will trigger before the token ceases to exist.)
111.7.proposition: Token death fires dies triggers BEFORE the token ceases to exist.

111.8.excerpt: A token that has left the battlefield can't move to another zone or come back onto the battlefield. If such a token would change zones, it remains in its current zone instead. It ceases to exist the next time state-based actions are checked.
111.8.proposition: Sacrificed/consumed tokens never become graveyard cards; they vanish at next SBA check.

113.7a.excerpt: Once activated or triggered, an ability exists on the stack independently of its source. Destruction or removal of the source after that time won't affect the ability.
113.7a.proposition: Stack abilities are source-independent (Kokusho/Artist triggers survive their sources).

116.2b.excerpt: Turning a face-down creature face up is a special action. A player can take this action any time they have priority.
116.2b.proposition: Morph turn-up uses no stack and cannot be responded to (with 702.37e).

117.4/608.1.excerpt: If all players pass in succession ... the spell or ability on top of the stack resolves ... (608.1: Each time all players pass in succession, the spell or ability on top of the stack resolves.)

118.8.excerpt: An additional cost is a cost listed in a spell's rules text ... that its controller must pay at the same time they pay the spell's mana cost ... (118.8a: announced per 601.2b.)
118.8.proposition: Altar's Reap sacrifice is a mandatory additional cost paid during casting (601.2f/h).

118.9.excerpt: An alternative cost is a cost listed in a spell's text ... that its controller may pay rather than paying the spell's mana cost. ... 'You may cast [this object] without paying its mana cost.' (118.9a: only one alternative cost per casting; announced per 601.2b.)
118.9.proposition: Force of Will pitch and Fierce Guardianship free-cast are alternative costs; gated on their conditions (blue card in hand / control a commander). CORRECTS RQ-C1 '602' citation (602 = activating activated abilities).

122.2.excerpt: Counters on an object are not retained if that object moves from one zone to another. The counters are not 'removed'; they simply cease to exist.
122.2.proposition: Blinked Bear's +1/+1 counter ceases; nothing moves it.

202.3.excerpt: The mana value of an object is a number equal to the total amount of mana in its mana cost, regardless of color.
202.3.proposition: Runeclaw Bear ({1}{G}) has mana value 2: Reanimate costs P0 2 life.

305.6.excerpt: An object with the land card type and a basic land type has the intrinsic ability '{T}: Add [mana symbol]' ... For ... Islands, {U} ...
305.6.proposition: Island's {U} ability is intrinsic and confers no color (with 105.2: Island is colorless).

400.7.excerpt: An object that moves from one zone to another becomes a new object with no memory of, or relation to, its previous existence.
400.7.proposition: Zone-changed objects (exiled-then-returned Bear, reanimated Bear, flickered Bear) are new objects; Auras/counters do not follow.

508.1.excerpt: 508.1g-j: optional costs to attack are chosen, total attack cost determined and locked in, mana abilities may be activated, then costs paid (508.1c-d: restrictions/requirements legality).
508.1.proposition: Propaganda's per-creature {2} is an attack cost paid per creature attacking P0; attacking P2 is untaxed.

509.1.excerpt: 509.1a-g: defending player chooses blockers and one attacker per blocker (restrictions/requirements checked; costs paid). 509.1h: blocked/unblocked status persists.
509.1.proposition: Double-block declaration procedure; no ordering sub-decision exists in current CR.

510.1.excerpt: 510.1c: A blocked creature assigns its combat damage to the creatures blocking it ... divided as its controller chooses among them. 510.1e: the total assignment is checked for legality. 510.2: assigned damage is dealt simultaneously.
510.1.proposition: Damage division is a free chooser-division (no blocker-ordering decision in current CR); trample adds the 702.19b lethal-first constraint for rollover.

601.2.excerpt: 601.2b: modal choice, alternative/additional-cost intentions, and X announced during proposal. 601.2c: targets announced at proposal (abilities triggering on becoming targeted trigger now). 601.2d: division among targets announced; each target gets at least one. 601.2f-h: total cost determined, locked in, then paid (601.2h orders non-random before random/library costs).
601.2.proposition: Casting pipeline: proposal (modes/costs/X/targets/division) then locked cost then payment. Fireball X=5/2-targets costs 7; Rolling Thunder X=4 division announced (6 ordered 2/1/1-class divisions); Cryptic modes+targets at proposal.

603.3.excerpt: 603.3a: trigger controlled by whoever controlled its source when it triggered (delayed: 603.7d-f). 603.3b: multiple triggers stack in APNAP order, each controller ordering their own. 603.3d: targets/mode-like choices for triggers follow 601.2c-d on stacking; no legal choice = removed from stack.
603.3.proposition: APNAP stacking + intra-controller ordering (5 Wardens; Artist+Kokusho); Artist target chosen at stacking.

603.4.excerpt: A triggered ability may read 'When/Whenever/At [trigger event], if [condition], [effect].' ... checks ... when the trigger event occurs ... triggers only if it is; ... checks the stated condition again as it resolves. ... This rule is referred to as the 'intervening if clause' rule. (CR example uses Felidar Sovereign verbatim: trigger at 40, Bolt to 37, resolution recheck fails, no win.)
603.4.proposition: Felidar Sovereign gates at creation AND resolution; flipping to 37 in response yields no win.

603.5.excerpt: Some triggered abilities' effects are optional (they contain 'may' ...) ... The choice is made when the ability resolves.
603.5.proposition: Braids may-sacrifice and Delina may-roll-again are resolution-time choices, not stacking choices.

603.7.excerpt: 603.7a: delayed triggers are created during resolution of spells/abilities (won't trigger before creation). 603.7b: fire once at next trigger event. 603.7c: object-change tolerance for the referenced object (with 400.7 new-object cutoff). 603.7d: spell-created delayed ability is controlled by whoever controlled the spell as it resolved.
603.7.proposition: Flickerwisp's return trigger is created at ETB resolution, controlled by P0, fires next end step; Bear returns as a new object.

603.10.excerpt: Normally, objects existing immediately after an event are checked for trigger matches; exceptions 'look back in time': 603.10a lists leaves-the-battlefield abilities (CR example: simultaneous mass-destruction fires a dies ability twice, including for itself).
603.10.proposition: Simultaneous-death triggers (Artist on Wrath; Artist on Kokusho; token-death) fire including for themselves; LKI look-back.

608.2.excerpt: 608.2a: intervening-if rechecked (fails = removed, does nothing). 608.2b: targets rechecked (all illegal = doesn't resolve; spell to owner's graveyard; partial legality resolves as much as possible). 608.2c: instructions followed in written order. 608.2d: resolution-time choices announced during application. 608.2e: multi-player choices in APNAP order, actions simultaneous. 608.2n: instant/sorcery to owner's graveyard as final part of resolution.
608.2.proposition: Resolution audit spine: recheck-if, recheck-targets (D04 fizzle), written order (D01 modes, D05/D06), APNAP multi-player (G05), graveyard after (D02/D03).

613.1/613.4/613.7.excerpt: 613.1a-g: layers apply in order (1 copy, 2 control, 3 text, 4 type, 5 color, 6 abilities, 7 P/T). 613.4a-e: within layer 7, sublayers 7a (CDA) < 7b (base-setting) < 7c (modification) < 7d (switch). 613.7: timestamp orders WITHIN a layer/sublayer only. (CR 613.4 Gray Ogre example: 0/1-setting + bonuses stack to 5/8.)
613.1/613.4/613.7.proposition: Clone copies in layer 1 before Humility strips (layer 6) and sets 1/1 (layer 7b): 1/1 no abilities regardless of timestamps (H01). Frog (7b base 1/1) always precedes Growth (7c +3/+3): 4/4 BOTH orders; H02 PATH_A 1/1 contradicted (with official Frog ruling).

614.1/614.4.excerpt: 614.1a: 'instead' marks replacement effects. 614.1c-d: enters-with/enters-as are replacement effects. 614.4: replacement effects must exist before the event (shields created in response resolve first).
614.1/614.4.proposition: Rest in Peace exile-instead; regeneration shields must pre-exist destruction; Stonecoil enters-with-X is replaceable (A04).

615.1.excerpt: 615.1a: 'prevent' marks prevention effects, watching for damage events (with 614-like continuous application).
615.1.proposition: Fog is prevention (not replacement/trigger): all combat damage prevented, no other state change.

616.1.excerpt: 616.1: if 2+ replacement/prevention effects would modify an event affecting an object/player, the affected object's controller (or owner) or the affected player chooses one to apply (616.1e: any may be chosen; 616.1f: repeat until none left). APNAP for simultaneous choosers.
616.1.proposition: P0 orders Doubling Season vs Hardened Scales (2 legal orders; 8 vs 7); single-shield A03 has no ordering choice.

700.2.excerpt: 700.2: modal = bulleted options (700.2a-b: modes chosen at proposal/stacking; illegal modes unchoosable). 700.2c: mode-gated targets chosen only if that mode chosen. 700.2d: same mode normally not choosable twice.
700.2.proposition: Cryptic: 6 two-mode combos, per-mode targets, resolution in mode order (with 608.2c). Casualties: 31 nonempty subsets (2^5-1).

700.4.excerpt: The term dies means 'is put into a graveyard from the battlefield.' (No exceptions in current text.)
700.4.proposition: Dies = battlefield-to-graveyard movement, including simultaneous self-death (K01), token death (I03), legend-rule transit (K02 same-controller variant).

701.8.excerpt: 701.8a: to destroy a permanent, move it from battlefield to owner's graveyard. 701.8b: destruction only via 'destroy' effects or lethal-damage/deathtouch SBAs. 701.8c: regeneration replaces destruction (see 701.19).
701.8.proposition: Destroy pipeline; Wrath legality; regeneration-replacement hook.

701.9.excerpt: 701.9a: discard = owner's hand to their graveyard. 701.9b: default chooser is the affected player; EXCEPTIONS: random discard or another-player-chooses.
701.9.proposition: Hymn's at-random discard is an explicitly allowed non-chooser discard: Rules-RNG selection, no hidden-choice offered. Duress is the another-player-chooses shape (P0 chooses from revealed hand).

701.19.excerpt: 701.19a: a resolving regeneration effect creates a shield: 'The next time [permanent] would be destroyed this turn, instead remove all damage marked on it and its controller taps it. If it's an attacking or blocking creature, remove it from combat.' 701.19c: creating a shield is not regenerating; 'can't be regenerated' stops application, not activation. CORRECTS RQ-C1 '702.13' (702.13 = Intimidate in this baseline).
701.19.proposition: A03 shield mechanics; application is automatic once the shield exists (no may/decline in current text).

701.20.excerpt: 701.20a: To reveal a card, show that card to ALL players for a brief time ... for as long as necessary to complete the parts of the effect that card is relevant to.
701.20.proposition: Duress reveals P1's hand to ALL players (not P0-only): RQ-C1 F02 hidden-info expectation contradicted; post-resolution knowledge is retained (no memory-wipe rule).

701.22.excerpt: 701.22a: scry N = look at top N, split bottom/top in any order. 701.22c: simultaneous multi-player scry decided in APNAP order.

701.23/701.24.excerpt: 701.23a: searcher looks at all cards in the zone. 701.23b: hidden-zone search for a stated quality MAY fail to find (even if present). 701.23e: found cards revealed only if instructed. 701.24a: shuffle = randomize so no player knows the order. CORRECTS RQ-C1 '701.19b' (701.19b = static-regenerate in this baseline).
701.23/701.24.proposition: Rampant Growth: searcher-only visibility, fail-to-find offerable, found land enters tapped, shuffle. Cultivate drawing two follows the same spine.

701.38.excerpt: 701.38a: to vote, each player, starting with a specified player and proceeding in turn order, chooses one of the listed choices. (Number supplied by RQ-C2; RQ-C1 cited voting rules without a number.)
701.38.proposition: Council's Judgment: open turn-order votes starting with P0 ('Starting with you'); Oracle exiles most-votes plus ties; 6 official rulings (no abstain, no targets, vote happens during resolution).

702.2.excerpt: 702.2b: toughness>0 creature dealt damage by a deathtouch source since last SBA check is destroyed (704.5h). 702.2c: nonzero deathtouch combat damage counts as lethal for excess-damage purposes.
702.2.proposition: E03 mutual destruction: 1 deathtouch damage destroys Bear; 2 damage destroys 1/2 Recluse.

702.19.excerpt: 702.19b: trample controller first assigns damage to blockers; once ALL blockers have lethal assigned, excess goes to blockers/player as controller chooses (accounting marked + same-step assigned damage). Need not max blockers, but then nothing may go to the player.
702.19.proposition: E02: scripted 2-to-Bear/1-to-Elves/4-to-P0 satisfies 702.19b (other compliant divisions also legal; no ordering decision exists).

702.37/708.excerpt: 702.37c: morph cast = 2/2 face-down, no text/name/subtypes/mana cost, {3} alternative cost. 702.37e + 116.2b: turn face up any time with priority as a special action (no stack). 708.2: face-down objects have only the listed characteristics. 708.5: only the controller may look at their face-down permanents. CORRECTS RQ-C1 '702.36' (702.36 = Fear in this baseline).
702.37/708.proposition: Willbender: hidden 2/2 until turn-up, unrespondable {1}{U} turn-up, turn-up trigger retargets Bolt (603.3d legality) to Elves.

704.3/704.5.excerpt: 704.3: SBA check precedes each priority grant; performed simultaneously as one event; triggers wait until checks complete. 704.5d: off-battlefield token ceases. 704.5f: toughness<=0 to graveyard (no regen). 704.5g: lethal damage destroys (regen replaces). 704.5h: deathtouch damage destroys (regen replaces). 704.5j: same-player 2+ same-name legendaries: controller keeps one, rest to owners' graveyards ('legend rule'). 704.5m: unattached/illegally-attached Aura to owner's graveyard.
704.3/704.5.proposition: SBA spine: K02 same-controller gating (704.5j condition fails across controllers); K01/I03/E03 destruction routing; I01 Pacifism to P1 graveyard. CORRECTS RQ-C1 '704.5c-adjacent' for commander damage (704.5c = poison; commander loss is 903.10a).

705.excerpt: 705.1: coin = two-sided object, equal likelihood; substitutes allowed by agreement. 705.2: flipper calls heads/tails (for win/loss effects); only the flipper wins/loses. (Mana Crypt ruling 2020-08-07: no actions between flip result and damage.)
705.proposition: J01: controller flips, win/loss determined, loss path deals 3 atomically; journal shape is engineering, not Rules.

706.excerpt: 706.1-706.1a: specified die, N equally-likely outcomes 1..N (d20 = 1-20). 706.3-706.3c: results tables map ranges to effects; 'Roll again' re-rolls same dice. 706.2: natural vs final (modifiers).
706.proposition: J02: d20 roll, 17 in Delina's 15-20 roll-again band (Oracle); 'may roll again' optional (603.5 + 2021 ruling); token copy + end-of-combat exile per Oracle.

707.2/707.3/707.10.excerpt: 707.2: copies acquire copiable values (+ stack choices). 707.10: spell copy = new stack object (not cast), copies modes/targets/X/costs; controlled/owned by the player who put it there; 707.10c: new targets allowed only if stated, and must be legal. 707.10a: off-stack copies cease (704.5e).
707.2/707.3/707.10.proposition: Twincast copy is P0-controlled, may retarget to P2 (legal), both spells to graveyard (608.2n). Phantasmal Image/Clone enter-as-copy (614.1c) with copiable values.

800.4.excerpt: 800.4a: leaving player: owned objects leave with them; control-granting effects end; noncard stack objects they controlled cease; remaining controlled objects exiled. NOT a state-based action; immediate. (CR example: Mind Control leaves with Alex; Assault Griffin reverts to Bianca.) 800.4b-d: no control hand-off to departed players; orphaned control ends in exile; departed players' triggers never stack.
800.4.proposition: G04 mechanically determined: P0-owned Control Magic leaves with P0; P1-owned Bear stays under P1. Stack empty; no triggers; SBAs resume normally after.

903.8/903.9a/903.10a.excerpt: 903.8: commander cast from command zone costs +{2} per previous cast from there ('commander tax'). 903.9a: commander in graveyard/exile since last SBA check: owner MAY put it into the command zone (an SBA). 903.10a: 21+ combat damage from the same commander = loss (an SBA).
903.8/903.9a/903.10a.proposition: G02: graveyard-vs-CZ offer + 8+2=10 recast (Ghalta costs {5}{G}{G}{G}=8, verified). G03: 12+12=24 >= 21 loss; only the pre-seeded ledger's legitimacy needs Sol (fixture design, not Rules text).

stale_reference_notes.602-as-costs: RQ-C1 Q-C01 cited '602 alternative/additional costs family'. In this baseline 602 = Activating Activated Abilities. Correct provisions: 118.9 (alternative) / 118.8 (additional) + 601.2b/f.
stale_reference_notes.701.19b-as-search: RQ-C1 Q-F01 cited '701.19b' for fail-to-find. In this baseline 701.19b = static-ability regenerate. Correct provisions: 701.23b (fail-to-find) + 701.23a/e + 701.24a.
stale_reference_notes.702.13-as-regenerate: RQ-C1 Q-A03 cited '702.13 (regenerate reminder semantics)'. In this baseline 702.13 = Intimidate. Correct provision: 701.19 (Regenerate).
stale_reference_notes.702.36-as-morph: RQ-C1 Q-F03 cited '702.36 (morph)'. In this baseline 702.36 = Fear. Correct provision: 702.37 (Morph) + 708 + 116.2b.
stale_reference_notes.704.5c-as-commander-damage: RQ-C1 Q-G03 cited commander-damage loss as '704.5c-adjacent'. In this baseline 704.5c = poison counters. Correct provision: 903.10a.
